transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Start: 16:00 PT
End: 16:46 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (BlueHarbor CTO), Priya Rao (Head of MLOps), Omar Diaz (Infra PM)

Summary (auto): Renewal & expansion check-in. BlueHarbor needs additional capacity and EU region; exploring Dedicated pool vs Hosted with egress controls. Agree next steps for pricing and benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood here, with Lena on the call. How's it going Mark, Priya?
[00:05] Mark: Hey Samir, hey Lena. Good, busy quarter. We'll try to keep it focused, we have procurement times to hit.
[00:12] Samir: Great. Agenda — quick recap of current committed capacity, proposed uplift, EU onboarding plan, pricing options, and open security questions.
[00:22] Priya: Sounds good. We need to make sure EU residency is non-negotiable, and we need a clear idea of latencies for EU traffic. Also want to see how burst capacity would look.
[00:34] Lena: Totally. We'll show some p50/p95 numbers for our Dedicated pool and how caching affects per-token cost. Quick note — some of the product terms might show up in the transcript weirdly, I might say "dedicate" sometimes, apologies.
[00:45] Omar: No worries. Also curious about model variants — are you recommending quantized models for the EU load to save cost?
[00:50] Lena: For the majority of BlueHarbor's use-cases (short prompt insurance quote generation + claim triage) quantized LLMs are usually fine. We can run a quality regression in the benchmark.
[01:08] Samir: To set context — current commit is a 4-GPU Dedicated pool, average token throughput 1.2M/day. The forecast you shared last month suggests a 3x peak in Q3. So we're discussing both capacity uplift and contract term changes.
[01:30] Mark: Yup. The 3x is peak days during open enrollment, so sustained bursts for a week maybe. We also want regional separation for EU customers — can't cross-store EU PII outside region.
[01:44] Priya: We have compliance reviewers who will want KMS/HSM details and an audit log stream. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:52] Lena: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) in Private and Dedicated, and we can emit audit logs to a customer S3/Kafka endpoint for retention. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[02:12] Samir: On pricing — we can present a 12-month renewal with a modest uplift and a 24-month committed plan that reduces unit cost and includes guaranteed burst capacity. We'll send both options after this call.
[02:33] Omar: Procurement will prefer a longer term if price delta is significant. How much of a drop are we talking?
[02:40] Samir: Ballpark — committing to 24 months and a slightly higher baseline might reduce per-token cost by 15-22% depending on quantization and caching. Exact numbers in the sheet.
[02:55] Priya: We need to evaluate latency — can you share p95 for EU Dedicated vs Hosted across typical 256 token responses?
[03:03] Lena: Sure. Practically, Dedicated in eu-west gives us p95 in the 180-250ms range for that profile, Hosted multi-tenant can be 220-350ms depending on load. We'll run a controlled benchmark.
[03:22] Mark: Those numbers are acceptable if consistent. Peak spikes are the killer. If Dedicated gives a consistent tail, that's attractive.
[03:30] Samir: Agreed. Also worth noting our smart routing — requests can failover to other regions or to a cheaper variant if capacity is constrained, but that may affect residency so we need to lock routing for EU traffic.
[03:47] Priya: Right, failover outside EU not allowed. We need explicit routing policy — EU traffic stays in-eu even if overload. Can Redwood support that?
[03:55] Lena: Yes, we can pin region-by-customer and configure fallback to identical EU model variants. We'll document this in the rollout config.
[04:10] Omar: About the pilot — can we do a Dedicated pilot in eu-west for two weeks before committing? We'll need to run synthetic load and some production shadow traffic.
[04:18] Samir: We can do a pilot, yes — standard is a two-week Dedicated pilot with a baseline commit or trial credits applied. We'll outline the pilot terms.
[04:28] Mark: Procurement will probably push to shorten signature time; any flexibility on mid-cycle termination for major incidents?
[04:36] Samir: We can include SLA credits and a defined incident window in the contract. Termination clauses typically depend on enterprise legal review but we'll try to be flexible.
[04:45] Priya: On encryption — we need BYOK/KMS integration with our AWS KMS; do you support key rotation and envelope encryption?
[04:53] Lena: Yes, we support BYOK via AWS KMS for Dedicated and Private. We do envelope encryption and can align rotation policies with your schedule. We'll capture the exact API and certs in the security docs.
[05:05] Samir: Let's talk numbers briefly. Based on your forecast, a 3x peak means targeting a 12 GPU Dedicated pool with ability to burst to 16 for 48h windows. Does that align?
[05:16] Mark: Yes that's roughly where we're headed, though maybe 10 baseline with a 16 burst. We want a small buffer for unexpected spikes.
[05:23] Lena: Fine, for cost modeling I'll include a 10 baseline / 16 burst scenario and a 12 baseline / 20 burst as conservative. We'll also show the Hosted equivalent cost.
[05:35] Omar: What about autoscaling speed? During spikes we need <90s spin-up for additional capacity, otherwise front-end queues back up.
[05:44] Lena: Autoscale is policy-driven. For Dedicated reserved pools spin-up is faster because hardware is already allocated, burst may rely on cloud provisioning which is 60-180s depending on region. We can configure pre-warming for predictable events.
[05:58] Mark: Pre-warming around open enrollment windows might be the best option. We'll share the dates.
[06:06] Samir: Great. For the benchmark — Lena, can you walk through what you'll need from BlueHarbor?
[06:12] Lena: We'll need a representative request profile (prompt lengths, token output distribution), concurrency targets, and any private model artifacts if you plan to use custom fine-tuned models. Also a list of test endpoints and a retention window for logs.
[06:28] Priya: We'll provide a CSV with token histograms and a small subset of anonymized prompts — can't share PII.
[06:35] Lena: That's fine. We'll run quality regressions and latency runs. We'll also test KV-cache warm/cold scenarios since insurance workflows often have repeated prefixes.
[06:47] Omar: One more thing: network egress costs for EU — if you're using cloud region eu-west, are egress costs to our infra included?
[06:55] Samir: Egress charges depend on deployment mode. For Dedicated in our managed service we typically include intra-region egress to your endpoints up to a cap; beyond that there are standard cloud egress rates. We'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
[07:07] Mark: Okay. Any regulatory paperwork? Data processing agreement?
[07:12] Samir: Yes we'll send the DPA and the SOC2 package. Also include details for data retention and deletion APIs.
[07:20] Priya: We need the retention API example — how to purge logs for a subject if requested.
[07:25] Lena: We have a purge endpoint; we'll add an integration example for S3 and for our audit log sink.
[07:35] Samir: Quick check — timeline. BlueHarbor wants production-ready EU handling by the start of Q3. That gives us about 10 weeks. Is that feasible?
[07:45] Mark: Yes, that matches our planning window — procurement by mid-April, pilot late April, provision production May/June, go-live early July.
[07:56] Lena: Technical ramp is tight but doable with parallel work: procurement/legal, security review, and a short benchmark. We'll highlight dependencies in the pilot plan.
[08:08] Omar: On license terms — are there minimum monthly commit equivalents? We need to map to our budgeting process.
[08:15] Samir: Yes, commit is expressed as baseline GPU pool hours or tokens/day equivalent — we'll convert to a monthly invoice line and show both GPU and token equivalence.
[08:27] Priya: We might have a constraint on capital vs operating spend; if you can provide 24-month with lower OPEX that helps.
[08:33] Samir: We'll show 24-month amortized vs 12-month. Also outline an option for a reserved capacity buyout if you want to mix capital commitment.
[08:43] Mark: Good. On SLAs — what does the uptime SLA look like for Dedicated?
[08:49] Lena: For Dedicated we offer a 99.9% service availability SLA with credits for downtime; network-related incidents are handled per region. We'll include specifics.
[08:58] Omar: Are you able to integrate with our SSO (Okta) and RBAC?
[09:03] Samir: Yes SSO via SAML/Okta and role-based access is supported; we'll include a one-pager on RBAC mapping for your teams.
[09:12] Priya: For the benchmark, can Redwood run in-region synthetic traffic from eu-west to eu-west? We want to avoid cross-region artifacts.
[09:18] Lena: Absolutely. We'll spin up test runners in eu-west; we'll confirm IP lists and any firewall rules you need to open.
[09:28] Mark: Let's lock on dates for the benchmark. If we get the CSV by Friday (March 21), when can you start?
[09:33] Lena: We can start March 24 and run for 3 business days to capture different load shapes.
[09:38] Samir: I'll follow up with two pricing options by March 20. Lena will take the benchmark plan and test scripts by March 24.
[09:46] Priya: Security follow-up — can we get a named security contact at Redwood for a direct sync?
[09:51] Samir: Yes, I'll introduce you to Priya B. (Redwood security) in that thread.
[09:58] Omar: Great. Anything else?
[10:01] Mark: One small ask — can Redwood provide a sample runbook for incident handling and response times?
[10:06] Lena: Yes, we'll attach a runbook example and an incident response SLA appendix.
[10:12] Samir: Perfect. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:18] [recap and quick readout of action items]
[10:45] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll send the pricing + security pack + benchmark plan.
[10:50] Mark: Thanks. Talk soon.
[10:52] Priya: Thanks all.
[11:00] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription mis-hearings (e.g., "dedicate" instead of "Dedicated"). External links shared: /docs/security-pack (sent after call), /sheets/blueharbor-forecast (customer-owned sheet).
